topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section establishes the lecturer introductions, scope, and overarching learning objectives for understanding the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Causation: Intrinsic vs. Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the biological nature of cancer development and evaluate the interplay between endogenous mutation risks, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and viral infections contribute to oncogenesis, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a key paradigm.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various dietary, chemical, and physical agents are metabolically activated to cause structural DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic drivers of cancer growth, focusing on chronic inflammation, the initiator-promoter concept, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Carcinogen Risk-Benefit Assessment and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarizes the core themes of the lecture and considers the everyday risk-benefit decisions associated with environmental exposures.
